name: Torcular
description: A star 86 parsecs away, 16 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 8198: radius 16.177 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 148.593 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.076) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 8198: effective temperature 5014 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.066)

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 8198: distance 85.69 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.057), at which the luminosity and radius hold

limb.none: no mass is measured and no spectroscopic surface gravity is published with this radius: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770 assume the gravity of their fit (table column 15)

text.card: A star 86 parsecs away, 16 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 149 times the Sun's luminosity at 5,014 K, so 16.177 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 8198: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: Omicron Piscium
quotes.card: Omicron Piscium is a binary star in the constellation of Pisces.
quotes.introduction: It is visible to the naked eye, having an apparent visual magnitude of 4.27.
